units.text: г) international treaties of the Russian Federation that have not entered into force.
units.label: Point «г» Part 2 Art. 125

units.text: 3. The Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation resolves disputes over competence:
units.label: Part 3 Art. 125

units.text: а) between federal bodies of state authority;
units.label: Point «а» Part 3 Art. 125

units.text: б) between bodies of state authority of the Russian Federation and bodies of state authority of its constituent entities;
units.label: Point «б» Part 3 Art. 125

units.text: в) between the highest state bodies of constituent entities of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Point «в» Part 3 Art. 125

units.text: 4. In the manner established by federal constitutional law, the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation reviews:
units.label: Part 4 Art. 125

units.text: а) upon complaints alleging violations of citizens' constitutional rights and freedoms, the constitutionality of laws and other normative acts referred to in points ‘а’ and ‘б’ of part 2 of this Article that were applied in a specific case, if all other domestic judicial remedies have been exhausted;
units.label: Point «а» Part 4 Art. 125

units.text: б) upon requests from courts, the constitutionality of laws and other normative acts referred to in points ‘а’ and ‘б’ of part 2 of this Article that are to be applied in a specific case.
units.label: Point «б» Part 4 Art. 125

units.text: 5. At the request of the President of the Russian Federation, the Federation Council, the State Duma, the Government of the Russian Federation or legislative bodies of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation interprets the Constitution of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 125

units.text: 5.1. The Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation:
units.label: Part 5.1 Art. 125

units.text: а) at the request of the President of the Russian Federation, reviews the constitutionality of draft laws of the Russian Federation amending the Constitution of the Russian Federation, draft federal constitutional laws and federal laws, and laws adopted in the manner provided for by parts 2 and 3 of Article 107 and part 2 of Article 108 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation before their signature by the President of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point «а» Part 5.1 Art. 125

units.text: б) in the manner established by federal constitutional law, decides whether decisions of interstate bodies adopted on the basis of provisions of international treaties of the Russian Federation interpreted in a manner contrary to the Constitution of the Russian Federation can be implemented, and whether a decision of a foreign or international (interstate) court or a foreign or international arbitral tribunal imposing obligations on the Russian Federation can be implemented where that decision conflicts with the foundations of the public legal order of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point «б» Part 5.1 Art. 125

units.text: в) at the request of the President of the Russian Federation, in the manner established by federal constitutional law, reviews the constitutionality of laws of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation before they are promulgated by its highest official (the head of its highest executive body of state authority).
units.label: Point «в» Part 5.1 Art. 125

units.text: 6. Acts or individual provisions thereof declared unconstitutional cease to have effect; international treaties of the Russian Federation that do not conform to the Constitution of the Russian Federation may not be brought into force or applied. Acts or individual provisions thereof declared constitutional in the interpretation given by the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation may not be applied in a different interpretation.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 125

units.text: 7. At the request of the Federation Council, the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation gives an opinion on whether the prescribed procedure has been observed in bringing charges of high treason or commission of another serious crime against the President of the Russian Federation or a President of the Russian Federation who has ceased exercising powers.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 125

units.text: 8. The Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation exercises other powers established by federal constitutional law.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 125

units.text: Article 126
units.label: Art. 126

units.text: The Supreme Court of the Russian Federation is the highest judicial body for civil cases, resolution of economic disputes, criminal, administrative and other cases within the jurisdiction of courts of general jurisdiction and commercial (arbitrazh) courts established in accordance with federal constitutional law and exercising judicial power through civil, commercial (arbitrazh), administrative and criminal proceedings. The Supreme Court of the Russian Federation exercises judicial supervision over the activities of courts of general jurisdiction and commercial (arbitrazh) courts in the procedural forms provided for by federal law and provides explanations on issues of judicial practice.
units.label: Art. 126 · text

units.text: Article 127. Deleted
units.label: Art. 127

units.text: Article 127
units.label: Art. 127

units.text: Deleted by an amendment to the Constitution of the Russian Federation (Law of the Russian Federation on an Amendment to the Constitution of the Russian Federation ‘On the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation and the Procuracy of the Russian Federation’) <24>.

units.label: Art. 127 · “<24> Article 127 was deleted in accordance with the Law of the…”

units.text: Article 128
units.label: Art. 128

units.text: 1. The Chairman, Deputy Chairman and judges of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation and the Chairman, Deputy Chairmen and judges of the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation are appointed by the Federation Council on the submission of the President of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 128

units.text: 2. Chairmen, deputy chairmen and judges of other federal courts are appointed by the President of the Russian Federation in the manner established by federal constitutional law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 128

units.text: 3. The powers and the procedure for formation and operation of the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation, the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation and other federal courts are established by the Constitution of the Russian Federation and federal constitutional law. The conduct of civil, commercial (arbitrazh), administrative and criminal proceedings is also regulated by the relevant procedural legislation.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 128

units.text: Article 129
units.label: Art. 129

units.text: 1. The Procuracy of the Russian Federation is a unified federal centralized system of bodies supervising observance of the Constitution of the Russian Federation and implementation of laws, supervising observance of human and civil rights and freedoms, conducting criminal prosecution within their powers, and performing other functions. The powers and functions of the Procuracy of the Russian Federation, its organization and operating procedure are determined by federal law.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 129

units.text: 2. Prosecutors may be citizens of the Russian Federation who hold neither foreign citizenship nor a residence permit or other document confirming a citizen of the Russian Federation's right to permanent residence in a foreign State. In the manner established by federal law, prosecutors are prohibited from opening or holding accounts (deposits) or keeping cash and valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 129

units.text: 3. The Prosecutor General of the Russian Federation and Deputy Prosecutors General are appointed by the President of the Russian Federation after consultations with the Federation Council and are removed from office by the President.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 129

units.text: 4. Prosecutors of constituent entities of the Russian Federation and prosecutors of military and other specialized procuracies equivalent to prosecutors of constituent entities are appointed by the President of the Russian Federation after consultations with the Federation Council and are removed from office by the President.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 129

units.text: 5. Other prosecutors may be appointed and removed from office by the President of the Russian Federation if federal law establishes this procedure for appointment and removal.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 129

units.text: 6. Unless otherwise provided by federal law, prosecutors of cities and districts and equivalent prosecutors are appointed and removed from office by the Prosecutor General of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 129

units.text: CHAPTER 8. LOCAL SELF-GOVERNMENT
units.label: CHAPTER 8. LOCAL SELF-GOVERNMENT

units.text: Article 130
units.label: Art. 130

units.text: 1. Local self-government in the Russian Federation ensures that the population independently resolves matters of local significance and possesses, uses and disposes of municipal property.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 130

units.text: 2. Local self-government is exercised by citizens through referendums, elections and other forms of direct expression of their will, and through elected and other local self-government bodies.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 130

units.text: Article 131
units.label: Art. 131

units.text: 1. Local self-government is exercised in municipal entities whose types are established by federal law. The territories of municipal entities are determined with regard to historical and other local traditions. The structure of local self-government bodies is determined independently by the population in accordance with the general principles of organizing local self-government in the Russian Federation established by federal law.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 131

units.text: 1.1. Bodies of state authority may participate in forming local self-government bodies and appointing and removing local self-government officials in the manner and cases established by federal law.
units.label: Part 1.1 Art. 131

units.text: 2. Boundaries of territories within which local self-government is exercised may be changed with regard to the opinion of the population of the relevant territories in the manner established by federal law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 131

units.text: 3. Federal law may establish special features of the exercise of public authority in the territories of cities of federal significance, administrative centres (capitals) of constituent entities of the Russian Federation and other territories.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 131

units.text: Article 132
units.label: Art. 132

units.text: 1. Local self-government bodies independently manage municipal property, prepare, approve and execute the local budget, introduce local taxes and levies, resolve other matters of local significance and, in accordance with federal law, ensure access to medical care within their competence.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 132

units.text: 2. Federal law or a law of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation may vest local self-government bodies with specific state powers, provided that the material and financial resources needed to exercise those powers are transferred to them. The exercise of transferred powers is subject to state supervision.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 132

units.text: 3. Local self-government bodies and bodies of state authority form part of the unified system of public authority in the Russian Federation and cooperate to resolve tasks as effectively as possible in the interests of the population living in the relevant territory.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 132

units.text: Article 133
units.label: Art. 133

units.text: Local self-government in the Russian Federation is guaranteed by the right to judicial protection and compensation for additional expenditure arising from the performance of public functions by local self-government bodies in cooperation with bodies of state authority, and by a prohibition on restricting the rights of local self-government established by the Constitution of the Russian Federation and federal laws.
units.label: Art. 133 · text

units.locator: CHAPTER 9. CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS AND REVISION OF THE CONSTITUTION
units.text: CHAPTER 9. CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS AND REVISION OF THE CONSTITUTION
units.label: CHAPTER 9. CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS AND REVISION OF THE CONSTITUTION

units.text: Article 134
units.label: Art. 134

units.text: Proposals to amend or revise provisions of the Constitution of the Russian Federation may be submitted by the President of the Russian Federation, the Federation Council, the State Duma, the Government of the Russian Federation, legislative (representative) bodies of constituent entities of the Russian Federation, and a group comprising at least one-fifth of the members of the Federation Council or deputies of the State Duma.
units.label: Art. 134 · text

units.text: Article 135
units.label: Art. 135

units.text: 1. The provisions of chapters 1, 2 and 9 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation may not be revised by the Federal Assembly.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 135

units.text: 2. If a proposal to revise the provisions of chapters 1, 2 and 9 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation is supported by votes of three-fifths of the total number of members of the Federation Council and deputies of the State Duma, a Constitutional Assembly is convened in accordance with federal constitutional law.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 135

units.text: 3. The Constitutional Assembly either confirms that the Constitution of the Russian Federation is to remain unchanged or drafts a new Constitution of the Russian Federation, which is adopted by the Constitutional Assembly by two-thirds of the total number of its members or submitted to a popular vote. In a popular vote, the Constitution of the Russian Federation is deemed adopted if more than half of the voters who participated vote for it, provided that more than half of all voters participated.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 135

units.text: Article 136
units.label: Art. 136

units.text: Amendments to chapters 3–8 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation are adopted in the manner provided for the adoption of a federal constitutional law and enter into force after approval by the legislative bodies of at least two-thirds of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Art. 136 · text

units.text: Article 137
units.label: Art. 137

units.text: 1. Amendments to Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, which determines the composition of the Russian Federation, are made on the basis of a federal constitutional law on admission to the Russian Federation and formation within it of a new constituent entity of the Russian Federation, or on a change in the constitutional and legal status of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 137

units.text: 2. If the name of a republic, territory, region, city of federal significance, autonomous region or autonomous area changes, the new name of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation must be included in Article 65 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 137

units.text: Section II. Final and transitional provisions

units.text: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
units.label: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

units.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
units.text: 1. The Constitution of the Russian Federation enters into force on the date of its official publication following the popular vote.
units.label: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS · “1. The Constitution of the Russian Federation enters into force…”

units.locator: SECTION TWO. FINAL AND TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
units.text: The day of the popular vote, 12 December 1993, is deemed the date of adoption of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.
